correctness.rationale: Deshpande–Singh Theorem 4.6 gives unique reduced homology degree q and rank. For each dihedral element, the signed augmented simplex action yields (-1)^(q+1) times its fixed-face orbit enumerator. For rotations, every invariant face is an admissible periodic binary word and the run automaton has exact characteristic polynomial (lambda^d-(-1)^d)/(lambda+1), yielding Z=(-1)^g(d 1_{d|g}-1). For reflections, folding gives intervals with exact u/v boundary caps; zero-separated run decomposition yields F_{a,b}=z(1+z)A_aA_b/(1-(-z)^d). All hypotheses and identity/axis edge cases are addressed. A separately constructed direct orbit enumerator passed 1200 cases and modular chain ranks passed 18; finite checks support but are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural family Ind_r(C_n), r>=2, already has a complete nonequivariant sphere-wedge classification, so identifying the full D_n rational representation is a motivated and nontrivial next invariant. The all-parameter character distinguishes rotation conjugacy/order behavior and the two even-n reflection axis types; e.g. (r,n)=(2,6) has rank one but rotation sign -1 and opposing reflection signs, information impossible to infer from Betti numbers. The short period-d interval series supplies a useful structural explanation and makes equivariant quotient-rational Betti numbers computable by character averaging.
